Ports with leading zeros (e.g. 'localhost:00080') are accepted as port 80; harmless for a loopback guard, but this case is untested
The reject table goes past the contract with 'localhost:0', 'localhost:65536' and leading/trailing-space rows, so the port-range check and anchoring are actually exercised

Existing e2e specs still assert the removed header surface (Sign out button, Account link): src/routes/header.e2e.ts, focus.e2e.ts, login/login.e2e.ts, account/password/change-password.e2e.ts, admin/users/admin-users.e2e.ts. They will fail after this change unless a sibling task removes or updates them; none is in this task's file list.
ARCHITECTURE.md:151 still describes a header with Account, Admin for admins, and a POST Sign out; it is now stale.

src/routes/account/password/+page.svelte still exists on disk, so the 'every nav link resolves to a route' test would not yet catch a leftover Account -> /account/password link until the sibling route-removal task deletes it. The self-check test probes /account/nonexistent, not /account/password, despite its name.

Removing alert.schema.ts and the per-user channel/watch signatures leaves e2e/seed.ts (inserts into alertChannel, watch rows with userId) and e2e/harness.e2e.ts (imports alertChannel, calls loadChannelConfig(db, key, design.id, 'ntfy')) broken; e2e is outside tsconfig so typecheck will not catch it, but `npm test` will fail until a sibling task rewrites them.

watches.ts insert switched from db.transaction to db.batch (to avoid SQLITE_BUSY on concurrent adds). The libsql batch is still atomic, and the id-collision test now proxies 'batch'. This is a behavioural change the task description does not mention.

0009/0010 only reject multi-user databases whose users collide on a channel kind or a product. A multi-user DB with disjoint kinds and products migrates silently and merges into one install. That matches data_scope ('unsupported') but is not a full refusal.

Channels sealed under the old per-user AAD survive 0009 but read as unreadable until saved again (documented in crypto.ts and tested in channels.spec 'legacy AAD or wrong key'). Upgraded installs will need their channel credentials re-entered.

0009's hand-added DELETE of config_enc IS NULL deliveries runs after the file's PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON. That is correct because the pragma is a no-op inside the migrator's transaction, and migrate.spec checks the result with pragma foreign_key_check.

The 'handle imports' assertion only collects specifiers from `from '...'` clauses. A bare side-effect import such as `import 'better-auth/svelte-kit'` would get past it, so the 'any subpath' contract line is enforced only for the named and type import forms.

The guard reads the Host header, not event.url, so it holds even when adapter-node builds the URL from ORIGIN. local-request.ts accepts exact loopback names only, with an optional port from 1 to 65535.

package.json still defines the admin:create script (node src/lib/server/cli/admin-create.ts) and the auth:schema script (--config src/lib/server/auth.ts --output src/lib/server/db/auth.schema.ts), both pointing at files this task deletes; the better-auth dependency also remains. Not in this task's file list, so presumably a sibling task (t-8), but they are dangling right now.

The route-matching and import-scanner fixture tests in removed-routes.spec cover parameter, optional and catch-all routes, layout groups, and every import form, so the scans of the real sources cannot pass by accident.

test_contract says any non-test file under src/ is scanned, but the removed-routes.spec glob only covers *.{ts,js,svelte}; a better-auth mention in src/app.html, src/lib/styles/*.css or src/lib/server/testing/fixtures/README.md would not fail it (none exists today)

playwright.config.ts still passes BETTER_AUTH_SECRET (E2E_SECRET) to the webServer env, and e2e/accounts.ts still has better-auth comments and the E2E_SECRET constant; harmless now that env.ts no longer declares the variable, and outside this task's files, but leftover
AUTH_TEXT's negative lookahead is case-insensitive, so identifiers like BetterAuthOptions are not caught by the text scan alone; only an import from better-auth would catch them

harness 'fresh seed' asserts the watch set equals SEEDED_WATCHES exactly, relying on test order; e2e/a11y.e2e.ts sorts before e2e/harness.e2e.ts, so the comment 'runs before every route spec' holds only while a11y stays read-only
'node-server needs a build' exercises the missing-entry guard via entry 'build/no-such-entry.js' rather than the default build/index.js; same branch, so it still guards the fail-fast path
nodeServerEnv spreads caller env last, so a spec can override HOST/PORT/DATABASE_URL/SCHEDULER_DISABLED; the allowlist from process.env is limited to PATH/SystemRoot/HOME as described
